analysis.title: 2027 Global Rates Outlook: A Better Buffer
key_insights: GS expects positive total returns in G10 government bonds in 2027, driven mainly by high starting yield levels (interest income). Price gains arrive later, once evidence of disinflation and a policy peak accumulates.
Year-end 2027 10y yield forecasts: UST 4.6%, Gilt 4.8%, Bund 3.1%, JGB 2.75%. The largest rallies are in USTs and Gilts, a smaller decline in Bunds, and a range-bound JGB.

Most G10 central banks are expected to deliver fewer hikes than markets price for 2027. By end-2027 the Fed, ECB, RBA and Norges Bank are expected to have started cutting, with the BoE following in early 2028. Japan is the exception, where GS expects more front-loaded BoJ hikes than the market prices.

The 2026 G10 bond selloff was sparked by the energy shock, then sustained by resilient growth, stable labor markets, a debt-financed investment boom and episodic fiscal worries. GS's baseline does not open up deeply lower yields but sees the risk of significantly higher front-end rates fading through 2027.

Duration has three supports: elevated starting yields, a less hawkish policy path than priced, and a better hedge against growth risks as inflation falls. Recent AI-related equity volatility has shown duration's diversifier role.

Curve view: steeper 2s10s curves in the US, Germany and UK, most pronounced in the UK because the gap between the market's policy peak and GS's terminal rate is largest there. The JGB curve should flatten as BoJ hikes mature. Longs are preferred in the 5y belly of US and German curves near term, because 2s5s tends to move sideways after the last hike.

Inflation pricing: the energy shock showed up as higher real yields in the US but as higher inflation pricing in the euro area and UK. GS favors long 10y TIPS against beta-weighted short 10y nominals in the US. In Europe and the UK it favors nominal longs in 1y1y or 1y2y forwards and inflation-curve steepeners, because front-end inflation pricing looks rich.
US breakevens have fallen more than their relationship with oil implies, amid AI-trade weakness and growth concerns. That leaves real yields cheap versus nominals.

Supply: net sovereign issuance stays elevated across the G4 in 2027, but net supply to the public levels out or falls in the US, euro area and UK. Japan is the outlier. Free float should rise 1-2pp of GDP in the US and UK, 4pp in Germany and 6-7pp in Japan.

Swap spreads: short Bund swap spreads should perform if sovereign spread concerns moderate, because rising German free float and normalizing sovereign credit erode Bunds' safe-haven premium. JGB swap spreads are biased tighter on wide valuations and heavy supply. Long-dated Gilt swap spreads are expected to widen modestly on a shorter issuance mix and slower QT. US spreads are better viewed as carry than as a widening trade.

US money markets: the Fed's reserve management purchases are expected to settle near $25bn a month from 2Q27, keeping reserves around 11% of bank assets with downside risk. The debt ceiling likely binds in 1Q27. A TGA decline of about $400bn would push SOFR down about 4bps, and the later unwinding could produce a sharper tightening in funding.

Euro area money markets: excess liquidity of about EUR 2tn is above the median preferred reserve level of about EUR 1tn. GS cautions that reserves can become a binding constraint earlier than surveys suggest and that demand grows with risk perception. It would look to engage ESTR-BOR basis wideners at a better entry point, with the ECB expected to be reactive on QT.

European sovereign spreads: energy relief could be worth about 20-30bp in 10y BTP-Bund spreads. GS forecasts 10y BTP-Bund at 105bp by mid-27 and 90bp by end-27, and 10y OAT-Bund at 130bp by mid-27 and 100bp by end-27. Spain's Bonos-Bund is forecast at 45bp throughout 2027. French political uncertainty may extend past the June parliamentary elections.

Rates volatility: the macro baseline points to lower rates vol and favors selling gamma. Implied vol sits at a substantial premium to fair value after AI disruption concerns and the US-Iran conflict. Growth scares are seen as the more potent source of vol upside, which argues for overlays such as long vega or 6m-1y expiry low-strike receivers on 2y-5y tails in the US.
GS favors selling EUR payers to fade 2027 ECB hike pricing. Euro rates vol is up about 70% of its 2022 increase despite much smaller moves in gas prices and yields.

US view: core PCE is forecast to fall from 3.2% at end-2026 to 2.4% at end-2027. GS expects two more Fed hikes, then a shift to cuts that likely starts by year-end 2027. AI build-out should limit yield declines in 1H27 and turn more balanced to bullish into 2028.

Other G10: BoJ expected to hike three more times by mid-2027 to a 2% terminal rate, with 2y JGB yields rising to at least 2%. BoE expected to hike once more to 4.25% in February. BoC two more hikes, RBNZ two more (February and June), Riksbank two more to 2.5%, and RBA cuts starting 4Q27. The SNB is expected to stay at 0% throughout 2027.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Front-end policy expectations do most of the work. Favorable inflation lets part of the 2026 reset in longer-term forwards reverse, implying positive total and excess returns.
A smaller decline than other markets because Bunds already embed a safe-haven premium and German supply is elevated.
Gilts have the highest sensitivity to energy prices and are the biggest beneficiary of energy relief, though fiscal trade-offs keep term premium sticky.
Range-bound as BoJ hikes and anchored inflation limit further term premium build, while the curve flattens.

macro_indicators.reading: 3.2% at end-2026 falling to 2.4% at end-2027
macro_indicators.interpretation: Fading tariff effects and a waning Iran-war energy boost support a shift in Fed risks from hikes toward cuts.

macro_indicators.reading: Two more hikes, then cuts starting by year-end 2027
macro_indicators.interpretation: GS economists are more dovish than end-2027 market pricing.

macro_indicators.reading: Three more 25bp hikes to a 2% terminal rate by mid-2027
macro_indicators.interpretation: Faster than the market, which prices the 2% terminal rate by end-2027, so 2y JGB yields should rise to at least 2% and the curve flatten.

macro_indicators.reading: Second and final hike to 4.25% in February
macro_indicators.interpretation: Policy normalisation resumes in 2028, dovish relative to market pricing, with risks skewed to further tightening.

macro_indicators.reading: Hike in December 2026 likely concludes tightening
macro_indicators.interpretation: A March 2027 hike is possible only if energy prices rise again. Energy relief later in 2027 should bring markets to price normalization.
Compression depends on the next French administration signaling credible deficit reduction.
Italy benefits most from energy relief, with tightening staggered behind falling rates vol and fiscal clarity.
Keeps reserves around 11% of bank assets and the Fed a source of bill demand.

trade_ideas.description: Long 10y TIPS versus beta-weighted short 10y nominal Treasuries
trade_ideas.rationale: Breakevens have fallen more than their relationship with oil suggests, leaving real yields cheap versus nominals.

trade_ideas.description: Long 5y belly in US Treasuries and Bunds
trade_ideas.rationale: After the last hike 2s5s tends to move sideways while the curve steepens further out, so belly longs insulate against hawkish risk without giving up disinflation upside.
The gap between the market's policy peak and GS's terminal rate is largest in the UK, and sticky fiscal term premium reinforces steepening.
BoJ hikes and evidence that inflation is anchored should let the excess steepness converge toward global peers.
trade_ideas.risk: Resurgent domestic fiscal concerns over JGB supply and demand.

trade_ideas.description: Long EUR 1y1y or 1y2y nominal rates and inflation-curve steepeners in the euro area and UK
trade_ideas.rationale: Front-end inflation pricing is rich to model fair value and GS expects it to compress as energy pressures ease.
Rising German free float and staggered sovereign credit normalization erode Bunds' safe-haven premium.

trade_ideas.description: Modest widening in long-dated (10y and 30y) Gilt swap spreads
trade_ideas.rationale: 10y spreads screen slightly cheap and 30y spreads benefit from a shorter issuance mix and slower BoE QT.
Spreads are on the wide side of fair value while free float rises 6-7pp of GDP.

trade_ideas.description: ESTR-BOR basis wideners, to be engaged at a more compelling entry point
trade_ideas.rationale: Excess liquidity is already below the upper end of plausible equilibrium reserve estimates and the ECB is likely to be reactive on QT.

trade_ideas.description: Overlay long vega or 6m-1y expiry low-strike receivers on 2y-5y tails in the US alongside short-gamma positions
trade_ideas.rationale: Downside growth scares are the clearest route to higher implied vol in 2027.

trade_ideas.description: Sell EUR payers to fade 2027 ECB hike pricing
trade_ideas.rationale: The ECB hiking cycle is likely to conclude after December, and sovereign stress acts as a speed limit on hikes.
trade_ideas.risk: Renewed upside in energy prices, with a March ECB hike a possibility.

trade_ideas.description: Position for SOFR to fall more than priced early in 2027 when the debt limit binds, ahead of risk of sharper tightening later
trade_ideas.rationale: A TGA drawdown adds liquidity and pushes SOFR lower, followed by tighter funding after resolution.
trade_ideas.risk: Unwinding of the liquidity boost after resolution could raise volatility, as in 2025.

trade_ideas.description: Long OATs for convergence toward fair value, with 10y OAT-Bund targeted at 100bp by end-27
trade_ideas.rationale: OATs trade about 50bp cheap on fair value metrics and should converge if the next administration signals credible deficit reduction.
trade_ideas.risk: Political uncertainty in France may extend past the June parliamentary elections.

risk_factors: Renewed energy price upside could revive hawkish policy pricing and trigger a March ECB hike.
Fiscal pressures in the US, UK, Germany and Japan limit how far term premium can fall.
US debt ceiling dynamics can create funding volatility in reserves, bills and SOFR.
Sovereign stress and declining excess liquidity in the euro area put ECB QT in focus.
Political risk from elections in France, Italy and Greece may stall spread compression.
AI-related pressures could keep a floor under US yields in 1H27, while an AI equity or credit wobble or growth scare could drive vol higher.
A risk-off move that strengthens the yen could threaten the BoJ policy path.
Resurgent fiscal worries about JGB supply and demand are the clearest JGB steepening risk.
Underlying inflation could prove hotter than expected, for instance in Australia.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 compares GS economists' 2027 policy rate change forecasts with end-2027 market pricing, showing GS more dovish than market pricing in every G10 market except Japan.
Exhibit 7 shows the 2s10s curve versus end-2027 forwards and GS forecasts, with the most pronounced steepening in Gilts and flattening in JGBs.
Exhibit 5 shows 10y UST annual excess returns versus 1y T-bills, with GS expecting positive excess returns in 2027 for just the second time since 2020.
Exhibit 19 shows OATs still trading 50bp cheap on fair value metrics, averaging 5 specifications.
vol_and_positioning: Implied rates vol across the USD and EUR surfaces is at a substantial premium to fair value after AI disruption concerns and the onset of the US-Iran conflict.
The macro baseline of moderating inflation and steady growth favors short-gamma strategies in 2027, overlaid with long-vega structures for broader risks.

In the US, 6m-1y expiries on 2y-5y low-strike receivers are suggested as a hedge against downside growth scares, which are seen as the most likely route to higher vol. The upward push on implied vol from rising yields has largely run its course.
In Europe, GS favors selling EUR payers to fade 2027 ECB hike pricing. The ECB hiking cycle ending and gradual non-recessionary cuts should return vol part of the way toward late-2025 lows.
Valuations in front-end USD swap spreads are fair while longer tenors are wide, so spreads are better viewed as carry than as a widening trade.
JGB swap spreads sit on the wide side of fair value with free float rising 6-7pp of GDP, biasing them tighter.
geopolitical: The US-Iran conflict and the resulting energy supply shock drove the 2026 inflation increase and bond selloff. GS's baseline assumes sustained energy relief.
Elections in France, Italy and Greece may stall or reverse sovereign spread tightening. French uncertainty may last past the June parliamentary elections.
Spain holds snap elections in November 2026, with polls showing a likely fiscally conservative administration.
US debt ceiling dynamics are expected to bind in 1Q27 and create funding and reserve volatility.
Winter weather and gas prices keep near-term right-tail risk in European rates vol.

tension_points.bull_case: High starting yields, fading hawkish policy pricing and falling inflation support positive total returns and restore duration's hedge value. GS sees the largest rallies in 10y USTs (4.6%) and Gilts (4.8%).
tension_points.bear_case: Renewed energy price upside, hotter underlying inflation, fiscal pressures (US, UK, JGB supply) and AI-related pressures in 1H27 could keep term premium and front-end yields elevated and delay price gains.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Renewed upside to energy prices, which GS says could bring a March ECB hike and a rebound in the recent rate decline in Australia.

tension_points.bull_case: Energy relief could tighten 10y BTP-Bund by about 20-30bp, and credible French deficit reduction could bring OAT-Bund to 100bp by end-27 given OATs trade about 50bp cheap on fair value.
tension_points.bear_case: Elections in France, Italy and Greece may stall or reverse tightening, and French political uncertainty may extend past the June parliamentary elections.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The next French administration failing to signal credible steps toward deficit reduction.

tension_points.bull_case: The macro baseline of moderating inflation and steady growth supports lower implied vol, favoring selling gamma and EUR payers.
tension_points.bear_case: A downside growth scare tied to AI disruption concerns is the more potent tail catalyst, and winter gas risks preserve near-term right tails in Europe.

theme_stances.key_argument: High starting yields, less hawkish policy pricing and falling inflation support duration and its hedge value.
theme_stances.evidence: Disinflation is the key ingredient to our constructive outlook

theme_stances.key_argument: The debt ceiling likely binds in 1Q27 and a TGA drawdown would push SOFR lower before a sharper tightening later.
theme_stances.evidence: Debt limit dynamics create room for SOFR to fall more than priced

theme_stances.key_argument: The benign macro baseline favors short-vol strategies, but growth scares are the more likely source of vol upside, so overlays are advised.
theme_stances.evidence: Macro baseline points to lower rate vol and favors selling gamma
